subject.title: Bug: Gateway falsely marks healthy local vLLM endpoints as timed out/overloaded, causing 1–23 min fallback cascades

question: Is there enough current-main live vLLM and gateway timing evidence to choose a fix, or should this remain blocked on maintainer live reproduction?
rationale: Source inspection shows multiple plausible owner boundaries and several partial fixes, but no current-main trace proves which remaining path still causes healthy endpoints to time out or the gateway RPC layer to stall.

options.title: Keep Live-Repro Gate
options.body: Keep this issue open and require a maintainer-run live trace before any new fix PR changes timeout, fallback, auth, cron, or gateway RPC behavior.

options.title: Queue A Narrow Fix
options.body: Promote a fix only if maintainers already have private current-main logs that isolate the owner boundary and can provide them to the repair lane.

options.title: Close As Partial Fixes
options.body: Close only if maintainers decide the remaining timeout and RPC symptoms no longer reproduce on current main or are covered by a separate canonical issue.

recommendation.title: Keep Live-Repro Gate
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require a maintainer-run live trace before any new fix PR changes timeout, fallback, auth, cron, or gateway RPC behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue is currently assigned to osolmaz and they are tied to the overlapping provider-auth prewarm fix path.
